conditions: Two points in an orthonormal Cartesian coordinate system in a Euclidean plane; coincident points are allowed.
spoken_aliases: d equals the square root of open parenthesis open parenthesis x sub two minus x sub one close parenthesis squared plus open parenthesis y sub two minus y sub one close parenthesis squared close parenthesis
distance equals the square root of the sum of the square of the difference of x sub two and x sub one and the square of the difference of y sub two and y sub one

evidence: The coordinate differences are perpendicular components of the displacement. Apply the Pythagorean theorem and take the nonnegative square root. The same formula gives zero for coincident points and the absolute component difference when one component vanishes.
